name: 4th Street Sweet Red
description: An easy-drinking sweet red from South Africa — soft, fruity and made for sipping.
details: A light, approachable red in the sweet style many people reach for when they want something smooth rather than complex. It's at its best lightly chilled, with spicy food or on its own.
tasting_notes: Expect ripe red-berry fruit and a soft, sweet finish.
food_pairing: Spicy suya and pepper soup, fried plantain, small chops, soft cheeses.
palate: Sweet and soft, with ripe red-berry fruit and gentle tannins.
serving_notes: Serve lightly chilled, around 12–14°C — 20–30 minutes in the fridge before opening.
cellaring_notes: Made to be enjoyed young. Buy to drink rather than to keep.

name: Chateau Vartely Muscat Red
description: A semi-sweet red Muscat from Moldova's Chateau Vartely — aromatic, fruity and gently sweet.
details: Chateau Vartely is a Moldovan winery. This demi-sweet ('demidulce') red is made from Muscat, a grape famous for its perfumed, grapey aromas, and it's easy to enjoy on its own or alongside spicy dishes.
tasting_notes: Perfumed and grapey, with floral notes and a gentle sweetness.
food_pairing: Spicy dishes, fruit-based desserts, puff-puff and chin chin.
nose: Perfumed and grapey, with the floral lift typical of Muscat.
palate: Gently sweet and soft, with ripe fruit flavours.
cellaring_notes: Best enjoyed young while the aromas are fresh.
producer_notes: Chateau Vartely is a winery in Moldova.
highlights: Aromatic red Muscat;Semi-sweet;Great with spicy food

name: Chateau Vartely Individo Merlot/Cabernet Sauvignon
description: A Bordeaux-style red blend from Moldova — plush Merlot fruit with Cabernet Sauvignon's structure.
details: A classic pairing of grapes: Merlot brings soft, plummy fruit and Cabernet Sauvignon adds structure and blackcurrant depth. Chateau Vartely's Individo range is made in Moldova.
tasting_notes: Plum, blackcurrant and a touch of spice, with a smooth, structured finish.
food_pairing: Grilled and roast meats, suya, beef stew, jollof rice with fried meat, hard cheeses.
nose: Ripe plum and blackcurrant, typical of the two grapes.
palate: Medium to full-bodied, with soft fruit and supportive tannins.
serving_notes: Serve at 16–18°C. In a warm room, give it 20–30 minutes in the fridge first; opening the bottle 15–30 minutes ahead lets it relax.
cellaring_notes: Enjoyable now; in Nigeria's heat, buy to drink within a year or two.
producer_notes: Chateau Vartely is a winery in Moldova; Individo is one of its ranges.
highlights: Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon blend;Smooth and structured;Made in Moldova

name: Chateau Vartely Individo Saperavi
description: A deeply coloured, full-flavoured red from Saperavi, the dark grape native to Georgia, grown in Moldova.
details: Saperavi's name comes from a Georgian word meaning 'dye', and it earns it: the grape gives wines of very deep colour, lively acidity and firm tannins. Chateau Vartely grows it in Moldova for its Individo range.
tasting_notes: Dark cherry, blackcurrant and pepper, with bright acidity and firm tannins.
food_pairing: Grilled and spiced meats, suya, goat, rich stews.
appearance: Very deep, inky red — Saperavi is known for its colour.
nose: Dark cherry and blackcurrant with a peppery edge, typical of the grape.
palate: Full-bodied, with lively acidity and firm tannins.
serving_notes: Serve at 16–18°C. In a warm room, give it 20–30 minutes in the fridge first; opening the bottle 15–30 minutes ahead lets it relax.
cellaring_notes: Saperavi has the acidity and tannin to age, but this style is best enjoyed over the next few years — and in a hot climate, kept cool.
producer_notes: Chateau Vartely is a winery in Moldova; Individo is one of its ranges.

name: Nederburg The Winemasters Shiraz
description: A ripe, spicy South African Shiraz from Nederburg, one of the Cape's best-known wine estates.
details: Nederburg has been making wine in Paarl since 1791 and is one of South Africa's most recognised names. This Shiraz is made for generous fruit, warm spice and easy, rounded drinking from the first glass.
tasting_notes: Dark plum and blackberry with black pepper and warm spice, and smooth, rounded tannins.
food_pairing: Suya, grilled beef, barbecued ribs, jollof rice with fried meat, mature cheddar.
nose: Dark plum and blackberry with black pepper and a hint of smoke, typical of Shiraz.
palate: Medium to full-bodied, with ripe dark fruit, warm spice and rounded tannins.
finish: Warm and spicy, of medium length.
serving_notes: Serve at 16–18°C. In a warm room, give it 20–30 minutes in the fridge first; opening the bottle 15–30 minutes ahead lets it relax.
cellaring_notes: Ready to drink on release. Keep it cool and enjoy within a couple of years.
producer_notes: Nederburg is based in Paarl in South Africa's Western Cape and has been producing wine since 1791 — one of the country's oldest and best-known wine estates.

name: Cederberg Merlot/Shiraz (Cederberger)
description: A soft, spicy Merlot and Shiraz blend from the high-altitude vineyards of South Africa's Cederberg mountains.
details: Cederberg Private Cellar is a family-owned estate high in the Cederberg mountains north of Cape Town, where altitude and cool nights give some of the country's most distinctive wines. The Cederberger blends Merlot's soft plum fruit with Shiraz's spice.
tasting_notes: Ripe plum and red berries with a touch of spice and soft tannins.
food_pairing: Grilled chicken and beef, suya, jollof rice, stews, soft cheeses.
nose: Ripe plum and red berries with a hint of spice.
palate: Smooth, medium to full-bodied, with soft tannins and dark-fruit flavour.
serving_notes: Serve at 16–18°C. In a warm room, give it 20–30 minutes in the fridge first; opening the bottle 15–30 minutes ahead lets it relax.
cellaring_notes: A 2017 wine is best enjoyed now rather than kept much longer.

name: The Chocolate Block
description: One of South Africa's best-known red blends — Syrah-led, plush and spicy, from Boekenhoutskloof.
details: The Chocolate Block is built on Syrah, with Grenache, Cinsault and Cabernet Sauvignon and a little white Viognier for perfume. It's a celebrated Cape red — rich and polished, with a reputation that has made it a go-to gift bottle.
tasting_notes: Dark berries, spice and a touch of perfume, with ripe fruit and silky tannins.
food_pairing: Grilled and roast meats, suya, ribs, mushroom dishes, rich pasta, mature cheese.
nose: Dark berries and spice, with a floral lift that Viognier typically adds.
palate: Rich but polished, with ripe dark fruit, spice and silky tannins.
serving_notes: Serve at 16–18°C. Decanting for 30 minutes helps it open up; in a warm room, give the bottle 20 minutes in the fridge first.
cellaring_notes: Delicious on release; in Nigeria's heat, keep it cool and enjoy within a few years.
producer_notes: Boekenhoutskloof is a leading Cape winery based in Franschhoek.

name: Cederberg Cabernet Sauvignon
description: A structured mountain-grown Cabernet Sauvignon from South Africa's Cederberg.
details: From Cederberg Private Cellar, a family-owned estate whose vineyards sit among the highest in South Africa. Altitude tends to give Cabernet freshness and tension rather than heaviness.
tasting_notes: Blackcurrant and cedar with a herbal edge, firm tannins and a long finish.
food_pairing: Grilled steak, suya, roast lamb, beef stew.
appearance: Expect a deep ruby with purple edges.
nose: Blackcurrant and cedar, with a hint of herbs, typical of Cabernet Sauvignon.
palate: Structured and dry, with firm tannins and dark fruit.
serving_notes: Serve at 16–18°C. Decant for 30 minutes; in a warm room, chill the bottle for 20 minutes first.
cellaring_notes: Cabernet of this calibre can improve for a few years if stored properly cool. In a hot climate, buy to drink.
